## Reading

Loukissas, Chapter 2, _A Place for Plant Data_, pp. 27–54. [Session 6](06-from-world-to-table.qmd) reads the same chapter from a different angle.

## Reading summary

Loukissas uses the Arnold Arboretum to show that data have complex attachments to place. Plant records are tied to living specimens, tags, collecting histories, institutional practices, maps, catalogues, and databases. Data can be **about**, **in**, and **from** a place. These relations shape how the records can be interpreted.

## In class

Students trace the relations between plant, place, label, record, database, and visualization.

## Output

A map of data-place relations.
